---
title: "Figure marks"
fig-pos: H
format:
  pdf:
    include-in-header:
      # The author redefinition the extension documents, and the only way a
      # principal locator is visible to `pdftotext`: bold and plain text
      # extract the same. `\newcommand*` lands above the extension's own
      # `\providecommand`, which then steps aside.
      text: |
        \newcommand*\quartoindexprincipal[1]{[P:#1]}
  html: default
  epub: default
  typst: default
filters:
  - index
---

The fixture for marks in a figure caption and in an image's alt text (M101).
Pandoc copies the caption of a figure into the alt text of the image it holds,
so a caption mark on a figure with no id reaches the filter twice (Quarto
empties the copy on a figure with an id); the copy must file nothing. A mark
an author writes in the alt text of an image that is not a figure's copy files
one locator at the image.

Every case but the last ends in an explicit page break, so the page each mark sits on is a
fact of this source: page 1 is this page, and each break starts the next.
`fig-pos: H` holds each LaTeX figure on the page its source puts it on. No
term below holds the letters `f` and `i` in a row, which the Typst floor sets
as one glyph.

A figure div with an id, whose image carries alt text that marks one term.
The backslash after the image keeps it from being the only content of its
paragraph, so Pandoc makes no figure of it and copies no caption into it:
